sources.entry: Node RED - Browser-based flow editor that helps you wiring hardware devices, APIs and online services to create IoT solutions. (Source Code) Apache-2.0 Nodejs/Docker
Node-RED | Flow-based programming for the Internet of Things

summary.one_liner: Node-RED is a browser-based, low-code flow editor for wiring together hardware devices, APIs and online services to build event-driven and IoT applications.
summary.what_it_does: Node-RED provides a browser-based flow editor for connecting hardware, APIs and online services as nodes in a flow. It is installed globally via npm and started with the node-red command, after which the editor is opened in a web browser. The README also describes a Node-RED Library with custom nodes and integrations, shared flows, and node collections. For developers, the repository can be cloned, built with npm, and run from source. The README mentions a forum, Slack channel and contributing guide, and says the project is maintained by its core team under the OpenJS Foundation.
use_cases: wire hardware devices to online services
connect APIs without writing much code
prototype home automation logic in a browser
how_to_run: Open the editor in a browser (URL shown in the terminal output)
git clone https://github.com/node-red/node-red (for development from source)
notable: Browser-based visual flow editor for wiring nodes together
Node-RED Library for custom nodes, shared flows and node collections
Installable globally via npm with a single command
Maintained as an OpenJS Foundation project
caveats: The README does not describe a Docker image or platform-specific setup; the awesome-selfhosted listing mentions Docker, which the README itself does not cover
Global install uses the --unsafe-perm flag, which the README includes without further explanation
